requirements.requirement: SIGHUP reloads message.conf in the existing writer process without terminating it or creating a second writer, and the writer continues appending the reloaded message.
requirements.summary: After SIGHUP, the PID and process start ticks were unchanged, exactly one writer remained, and the reloaded value appeared in subsequent journal entries.

requirements.requirement: An empty configuration is rejected while the writer retains and continues using the last valid message.
requirements.summary: With message.conf reduced to zero bytes and SIGHUP sent, the same sole writer stayed alive and appended two entries containing the previous valid message.

requirements.requirement: The writer exits cleanly on SIGTERM.
requirements.summary: The corrected bounded test observed the worker before SIGTERM, exit status 0 afterward, disappearance of the tested PID, and no remaining writer.

requirements.requirement: Existing journal entries are preserved and the current message continues to be appended.
requirements.summary: The original first entry remained unchanged, while line counts increased during operation and after reboot with exactly one active writer.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were unchanged before and after execution. The repaired program compiled under the installed /usr/bin/python and ran successfully before and after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are directly demonstrated. The provider-wide restart protocol also shows a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot scheduling and loss of connectivity, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovery with one active writer, preserved data, valid configuration, and ongoing appends.
limitations: There is no final recursive inventory or checksum of the application directory, so the exact final directory contents—and whether any residue exists beyond the observed worker.py.pre-repair backup—cannot be established.

Signal behavior was tested directly before reboot; the post-reboot evidence demonstrates recovery and continued writing but does not repeat the SIGHUP, empty-configuration, and SIGTERM behavioral tests.
Requirement req-4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Core changes were scoped, package health remained clean, no failed services or new listening sockets appeared, and the mandatory restart protocol was complete. Hygiene deductions: cmd-e3ed678737da4405 created worker.py.pre-repair and no later command removed it, so it appears to be retained backup residue; the first SIGTERM experiment in cmd-154db479afda420c produced exit 143 and was superseded by cmd-13990498eba44176, making its extra test-process mutation noncontributing, although the process itself was reverted; and evidence files created by cmd-b17014a91fbf46a8 plus the test log written by cmd-154db479afda420c and cmd-13990498eba44176 remained in /tmp after completion. These were bounded, low-risk residues rather than broad or security-weakening changes.
